name: Microspherophakia-metaphyseal Dysplasia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of microspherophakia characterized by small, spherical crystalline lenses
Radiographic evidence of metaphyseal dysplasia with irregular metaphyseal widening and flaring
Secondary ocular complications such as lens subluxation or glaucoma
Short stature with disproportionate limb shortening

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both microspherophakia and metaphyseal dysplasia confirmed by clinical and radiographic evaluation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Small, spherical crystalline lenses leading to refractive errors
Radiographic metaphyseal abnormalities with flaring and irregularity

common.notes: Partial dislocation of the lens often leading to visual impairment

common.symptomName: Short stature with disproportionate limb shortening
searchTerms: short height with uneven limb length

common.notes: Elevated intraocular pressure due to lens-induced angle closure
searchTerms: eye pressure increase from lens abnormalities

common.notes: Increased range of motion in multiple joints

occasional.notes: Nearsightedness due to altered lens shape
Skeletal maturation lagging behind chronological age
Irregular curvature of the cornea causing distorted vision

rare.notes: Opacification of the lens secondary to structural abnormalities

imaging: Radiographs showing metaphyseal flaring and irregularity
Ocular ultrasound demonstrating small spherical lenses
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with lens development and skeletal dysplasia (specific gene not well established)
other: Clinical ophthalmological examination revealing microspherophakia and lens subluxation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of brachydactyly and joint stiffness
Short stature with characteristic facial features
Ectopia lentis with elongated lenses rather than microspherophakia
Cardiovascular involvement such as aortic root dilation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive glaucoma leading to vision loss
Severe metaphyseal abnormalities causing skeletal deformities
Lens subluxation causing acute angle-closure glaucoma
references: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) entry on microspherophakia and skeletal dysplasias
Pyeritz RE. Microspherophakia and associated skeletal dysplasias. Am J Med Genet. 1995
